messages:
maya: Heads up — ap-southeast1 queue depth just skyrocketed for mosaic-13b-quant, likely due to the routing + network flaps. Seeing sustained backlog growth for last 18m.
sam: grabbing graphs now. link: https://grafana.redwood/ap-se1/queues
olivia: confirmed, queue went from ~120 to 1400. CPU on tokenizer pods is fine, GPU pods are saturated.
raj: any change in ingress traffic pattern? Did a partner ramp anything?
maya: partner spike + couple of customers moved traffic regionally (AP fallback) after an unrelated LB incident earlier. Noted more long-tail requests.
lee: quick metrics snapshot: ```
ap-southeast1 | model=mosaic-13b-quant | queue=1420 -> 320 in 15m | running_gpu_workers=48/64 | avg_token_latency=780ms | 95th_token_latency=1.6s
ap-southeast1 | model=mosaic-4b | queue=120 -> 30 | running_gpu_workers=12/12
```
sam: that mosaic-13b working set already has slow KV cache misses. With network flaps, retry tail amplifies queue.
olivia: we should triage per-model admission first. Recommend soft admission for mosaic-13b-quant in ap-se1 and divert new requests to mosaic-4b-quant where quality acceptable.
raj: +1. Also enable prefix-KV caching reuse for mosaic-13b variants (experimental policy) — will reduce tokens by ~12% based on recent evals.
maya: proposed immediate commands: 
```
# soft admission 50% new sessions for mosaic-13b-quant
redwoodctl admission set --region ap-southeast1 --model mosaic-13b-quant --new-rate 0.5 --mode soft
# add diversion to mosaic-4b-quant
redwoodctl route add --region ap-southeast1 --from mosaic-13b-quant --to mosaic-4b-quant --pct 30
```
lee: also propose raising preemption window to 90s to free slots for small fast requests. current preempt=30s is too short to reclaim.
sam: quick cost tradeoff: diverting 30% to mosaic-4b reduces GPU token-cost ~2.7x; but if we overflow to Dedicated cross-region it costs more. We should avoid cross-region fallbacks.
olivia: agree — keep traffic regional where possible. If admission doesn't stabilize in 20m, failover plan: move lower-priority customers to degraded-rate SLA and spin up two extra mosaic-13b nodes from reserved pool.
raj: I'll flip the caching flag and run a small canary on 10% of traffic.
maya: I'm executing the admission + routing commands now. will post results in 5m.
deploy-bot: started run: admission change (cmd id chg-20260320-01) by maya. status: in-progress.
lee: after admission, watch model-specific drop rate and routing success. Dashboard panels to monitor: queue_len, serve_rate, kv_hit_rate, per_model_latency.
maya: admission set done. diversion rule pushed at 30%.
sam: preliminary numbers after 6m: queue down to 760, running_gpu_workers jumped to 52/64, avg latency down ~20%.
olivia: nice. still seeing 200 requests stuck with long tail retries — need to purge stuck sessions after timeout.
raj: adding a short TTL purge for queued sessions > 120s. command:
```
redwoodctl queue purge --region ap-southeast1 --model mosaic-13b-quant --older-than 120s --dry-run
```
maya: run it for real now.
sre-oncall: purge executed. 188 sessions removed. we freed ~6 GPUs worth of work.
lee: post-purge queue = 320, latency back to acceptable (avg 420ms).
sam: action items: 1) make soft-admission policy templated for other regions, 2) follow up on partner fallback behavior to prevent regional stampedes, 3) schedule a capacity add in next maintenance window if partner growth is permanent.
maya: assigning: sam for policy template, raj for caching rollout, lee for purge automation runbook, olivia for SLA comms. I'll close this triage in 2h if stable. :thumbsup:
